name: Photophoretic-Trap Volumetric Display
definition: A free-space volumetric display that creates luminous image points in space using a trapped particle illuminated by RGB lasers, forming images via persistence of vision (POV). It solves the 'clipping' limitation of holographic displays where image points are physically separate from the scattering surface, allowing for unconstrained viewing angles and geometries like long-throw projections.
summary: The Photophoretic-Trap Volumetric Display creates free-space 3D images by trapping and illuminating a single particle with RGB lasers, enabling 360-degree viewing angles and unconstrained geometries unlike holographic displays.
